about: How the family reads the key the Pipelex login saved, executed by the initializer's suite and by the webapp-js template's, whose copy is scripts/lib/fixtures/login-key.json, written by the repository's make shared-files and never edited. Both readers follow pipelex-mcp's src/credentials.ts, which owns the file: PIPELEX_HOME's .env, or ~/.pipelex/.env, read only when the environment holds no key. Each case runs in a throwaway directory, written <root> below, whose home/ is the user's home directory.

legend.pipelex_home: The PIPELEX_HOME the reader is given, <root> standing for the throwaway directory. Absent: not set.
legend.file: Where something is put, as a path under <root>. Absent: nothing is put anywhere.
legend.kind: Instead of content: directory, a directory stands where the file would be; over-limit, a file of one byte more than the largest the reader reads, assigning a key.
legend.expect.status: key: a key was found; no-key: the file was read and holds no key; missing: there is no file; unreadable: something stands there that is not a readable file of at most the size limit; relative-home: PIPELEX_HOME is refused, and nothing is read.
legend.expect.key: The key found, with status key.
legend.expect.base_url: The file's PIPELEX_BASE_URL, which comes with its key alone; null when the file sets none or holds no key.
legend.expect.file: The file the reader looked at, as a message shows it: ~ for the home directory, <root> for the throwaway directory, / for the system's separator.

cases.name: the default home holds a key
the file's base URL comes with its key
a leading byte-order mark is not part of the first name
a file with a base URL and no key is no key, and its base URL is not taken
an empty key is no key
an absolute PIPELEX_HOME is read instead of the default home
an absolute PIPELEX_HOME with no file does not fall back to the default home
a PIPELEX_HOME starting with ~/ is under the home directory
a PIPELEX_HOME of ~ is the home directory itself
an empty PIPELEX_HOME is not set
a directory where the file would be is unreadable
a file past the size limit is unreadable
